charter.purpose: Project Atlas will document, approve, launch and assign an owner to every HR policy, process and legal obligation the company needs: 438 items in 13 jurisdictions, between Oct 12, 2026 and Oct 8, 2027. It turns the Atlas library from a researched working draft into the company's approved and evidenced set of HR rules. Employees and managers will know which rules apply to them and in which language, HR will run each process the same way in every country, Legal and Internal Audit will be able to show compliance item by item, and every item will have an owner who keeps it current after the program closes.
charter.problem: The company has grown into 13 jurisdictions faster than its HR documentation. Policies and procedures sit in different places and versions, many local requirements are met informally or through individual knowledge, and there is no single list of who owns each filing, notice, posting and control. Employment law in the company's footprint is changing fast: India's final Labour Code rules were notified in May 2026, Taiwan's workplace bullying rules took effect in July 2026, California banned stay-or-pay clauses from January 2026, and Washington voids all noncompetes from June 30, 2027. As a Nasdaq-listed semiconductor company, it also carries SOX-relevant HR controls, Board-approved Code, clawback and insider trading policies, and export-control duties for employees. Without a program the likely failures are missed filings and postings with fines, policies that cannot be enforced in Germany, China, Taiwan or Vietnam because consultation, filing or translation was skipped, discipline and dismissals that fail when challenged, audit findings on HR controls, and inconsistent decisions by managers. Each of these costs more the longer it waits.

inScope: All 438 items in the Atlas: 57 policies, 97 processes and 284 legal obligations.
The 13 jurisdictions: US federal; California, Colorado, North Carolina, Texas and Washington; Canada (Ontario and British Columbia); Germany with the EU layer; Israel; India; Taiwan; China; Vietnam.
Global policies and the country addenda each jurisdiction needs, written once and localized rather than forked.

Translations needed for enforceability or understanding: German, Hebrew, Simplified and Traditional Chinese and Vietnamese, plus local-language notices in India and the US where the law requires them.
Employee-representative information, consultation and co-determination, and the filings or registrations needed before an item takes effect locally.
Process documentation, including embedded controls and agreement of SOX-relevant HR controls with the SOX PMO.
Evidence that each legal obligation is met, with an owner, a cadence and the next due date.
Communications, manager toolkits, training and the global attestation campaign for new or changed items.
Updates to the 48 Atlas templates where an in-scope item changes them.
Approval chains, status tracking and evidence in the Atlas, and handover to business-as-usual owners with an annual review calendar.
outOfScope: Redesigning pay, bonus, equity or benefit plans. The program documents approved practice; design changes go through normal reward governance.
Negotiating collective agreements or works agreements beyond what a specific item needs to take effect locally.
New HR systems or reconfiguring Darwinbox, Greenhouse or the LMS, beyond publication links, assignments and acknowledgment reports.
Jurisdictions outside the 13, including Quebec and any new country or entity. Adding one needs an approved change request.
Non-HR policies such as finance, IT security and procurement, except the HR sections or links that in-scope items need.
Running the processes day to day, such as case handling, payroll runs or filings that fall due after handover.
Remediating past non-compliance such as back pay or late filings. Gaps found are logged and handed to Legal under privilege, and remediation is funded separately.
New features in the Atlas, which is already built. The program covers configuration and data upkeep only.
Legal opinions on questions not tied to an in-scope item.

approach: Risk first, in waves. Mobilize (Oct 12 to Nov 6, 2026) sets up the team, chains and a rated baseline. Waves 1 to 3 then take roughly 40%, 35% and 25% of each workstream's required items, ranked by legal and audit risk, which is about 170, 145 and 105 items. Policies go first in each wave so the processes, notices and controls that depend on them follow. Wave 4 covers the 17 best-practice items, the attestation campaign, audit readiness and handover.

One path for every item. Each item moves through Discover (2 weeks), Draft (3), Review (2), Approve (2) and Go live (1), and each stage has a definition of done. Start dates are staggered so every workstream has items in each stage at once and reviewers see a steady flow instead of a single peak.

Workstreams own content; cross-cutting teams make it work everywhere. Six workstreams organized by lifecycle domain own the items. Country implementation, legal review, change and communications, and the PMO serve all six, so local requirements, legal points and launch needs are built in during Draft rather than added at the end.

Start from the Atlas, not a blank page. Owners draft from the Atlas wording, templates, country notes and research, and from current company documents found in Discover. Contract writers and the policy editor put content into the standard template, which shortens drafting and keeps the style consistent.

Global text, local addenda, gates planned backwards. The English master is never forked by country; addenda carry the local differences. The country implementation forum plans consultation, filing and translation lead times back from each local effective date, and German works council information starts in Discover for any item that touches co-determination.

Work to the calendar. There are no approvals or launches in the year-end freeze (Dec 21, 2026 to Jan 1, 2027), so Wave 1 drafts are complete by Dec 18. APAC reviews and launches avoid Feb 5 to 14, 2027. The legal review board meets weekly during each wave's review peak. Legally mandated changes due before their planned wave, such as Vietnam's Culture Day holiday on Nov 24, 2026 or Washington's noncompete ban from June 30, 2027, take a fast-track path with the same approvals.

The Atlas is the single source of truth. Status, owners, approvals and evidence links live in the Atlas and the PMO reports straight from it. Final approved documents live in the policy repository. There are no side trackers.

Build for business as usual from day one. Each item owner is the long-term owner, each item gets a review date when it goes live, and the policy lifecycle governance process (DS-08) becomes the operating model. The attestation campaign and Internal Audit's sample test that this works before the program closes.
assumptions: Workstream leads, item owners and reviewers can give the time in the resourcing plan from Nov 9, 2026, and their managers have agreed to it.
The budget is approved at M02 on Oct 23, 2026, and the contractors and translation vendor are engaged by Nov 6, 2026; local counsel are engaged on existing panel terms.
The Atlas content (research completed in September 2026) is a usable starting draft, and local counsel can confirm points marked 'verify' without major rework.
Current company documents exist for most items and can be found during Discover; items with no document still fit the 3-week Draft stage.
Approvers act within 3 business days per step, and the CHRO can approve policies in batches.
Board committees meet at least quarterly and can approve the Code, clawback and insider trading policies at scheduled meetings or by written consent.
Darwinbox, the LMS and the e-signature tool can support publication links, assignments and acknowledgment reporting without a system project.
Employee representatives engage in good faith within normal timelines, and no Wave 1 item needs a conciliation board (Einigungsstelle) in Germany.
No acquisition, divestiture, new country entry or large restructuring changes the 438-item, 13-jurisdiction scope; if one happens it goes through change control.
The translation vendor returns a policy-length document in 5 to 7 business days per language, plus up to 3 business days for legal back-check.
constraints: Fixed dates: every legally required, public-company and semiconductor item is live with evidence by Aug 13, 2027 (M14), and the program closes on Oct 8, 2027 (M18).
Year-end freeze from Dec 21, 2026 to Jan 1, 2027: no approvals or launches. Wave 1 drafts must be in review by Dec 18, 2026 (M06).
Lunar New Year and Tet, Feb 5 to 14, 2027: China, Taiwan and Vietnam reviewers are away, so APAC Wave 1 launches finish by Feb 4 or need a steering committee deferral.

Local gates set the earliest local effective date: Germany's co-determination under §87 BetrVG (working time, monitoring tools, pay principles, bonus schemes, mobile work); China's democratic procedure and acknowledgment; Taiwan's work-rule filing (30+ employees) and labor-management meeting approvals; Vietnam's union consultation and registration of internal labour regulations; India's standing orders (300+ workers) where they apply.

The Board approves the Code of Conduct, clawback and insider trading policies. The insider trading and clawback policies are filed as Exhibits 19 and 97 to the Form 10-K, due about Mar 1 to Mar 31 depending on filer status, so approvals must fit the filing calendar.
Statutory effective dates do not move. A legally mandated change must be live by the law's effective date even if that is earlier than the item's wave.
Legal advice and local counsel memos stay privileged with Legal. The Atlas and the policy repository record only that legal review is complete, its date and its outcome.
Employment counsel is available at 0.5 FTE (0.7 in review peaks). There is no new permanent headcount; the PMO analyst, policy editor and writers are fixed-term contractors.
External spend stays within the approved envelope of USD 1.2 to 1.95 million including contingency; any increase needs sponsor and CFO approval.
The Atlas is the system of record for status and approval evidence, and documents are published only through the policy repository and Darwinbox links.

docStandards.standard: The Atlas is the system of record for each item's status, stage, owner, approval chain, approvals and evidence links. The policy repository (document management system and policy portal) holds final approved documents and translations. Working drafts live in the project folder in the repository. Status is never tracked in separate spreadsheets or email.

Policies use T-POLICY, including the header block, change log and addendum placeholders. Processes use the Atlas process structure: summary, trigger, swimlane, steps with timings, controls, RACI for deep dives, KPIs, variations and country notes. Obligations use the evidence record: requirement, citation, owner, cadence, evidence and next due date. Any departure from a template needs PMO approval, recorded in the Atlas.

Keep the Atlas ids: POL-NN for policies, process ids such as OF-01, and R-NNN or R-CC-NN for obligations. Country addenda add the jurisdiction code, for example POL-09-DE. File names follow ID_short-title_language_vVERSION_status, for example POL-09_anti-harassment_de_v1.0_approved.pdf, using the language codes en, de, he, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, vi, kn, te, es and fr.

Drafts are 0.1, 0.2 and so on, and the first approved version is 1.0. Editorial fixes that do not change meaning become 1.1, 1.2 and need only owner and PMO document-control sign-off. Any change to rights, duties, eligibility, amounts or process steps is a new major version (2.0) and runs the full chain. Every document keeps a change log with version, date, summary and approver.

Each document shows its approval date and global effective date, and each addendum shows its local effective date. A local effective date is never earlier than publication, translation and any consultation or filing for that country. Legally mandated changes take effect on or before the statutory date. No effective dates fall in the Dec 21, 2026 to Jan 1, 2027 freeze.

Policies are reviewed at least every 12 months (DS-08), processes at least every 2 years or after a system or organization change, and obligations on their statutory cadence. A change in law flagged on the Atlas watchlist triggers an earlier review. The next review date is set at Go live and appears in the annual review calendar.

Approval records, redlines, comment logs, consultation minutes, filing receipts and attestation reports are kept for at least 7 years after the document is superseded, or longer where the records retention schedule (DS-03, POL-49) or a legal hold requires. Superseded versions are archived read-only, never deleted.

English is the master. A professional vendor translates with a legal back-check, and each translation carries the master's version number and is published by the local effective date. Prevailing-language clauses follow the addendum: Chinese prevails in China, the Traditional Chinese version is the one relied on in Taiwan, and Vietnamese governs internal labour regulations in Vietnam. Minimum sets: German or bilingual core policies for non-English speakers and German postings in Germany, Hebrew notices and harassment bylaw in Israel, English plus Kannada or Telugu notices in India, and California EEO and harassment policies in any language spoken by 10% or more of a facility's workforce.

Write for the employee who must follow the rule. Use sentence case, active voice and sentences averaging under 20 words. Use 'must' for requirements and 'should' for guidance, define each term once, and keep policy statements separate from procedure steps. The policy editor checks every draft before Review, with a target reading level of grade 10 or below for employee-facing text.

Published documents meet WCAG 2.2 AA: real headings, tagged PDFs, alt text for diagrams with a text step list for every swimlane, enough contrast and no meaning carried by color alone. Accessible or alternate formats are provided on request, which Ontario's AODA requires (verify).

After approval, every change goes through a change request in the Atlas, classed as editorial (owner and PMO), minor (owner, workstream lead, and Legal if legal content changes) or material (full chain, communication and re-attestation where needed). Changes to project scope, milestones or budget follow the decision rights and the project document chain.

Only the current version is live in the policy repository and linked from Darwinbox. Copies on team sites, shared drives or intranet pages are replaced with links. Printed or downloaded copies are marked 'uncontrolled when printed'. Each document is classified Public, Internal or Confidential.

Each piece of evidence is linked from the item in the Atlas, named to the file convention, dated and shows who did what: approval records, published link and version, filing receipts, posting photos with date and location, communication copy and send date, and LMS assignment and completion reports. An auditor must be able to confirm the item without asking the owner.

Legal advice and local counsel memos stay in Legal's privileged files; the Atlas records only that legal review is complete, its date and its outcome. The Atlas holds no employee personal data beyond owner and assignee names, and acknowledgments stay in the LMS and HRIS.
